newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 25.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
** The Indian government on Monday announced a scheme for sale of foodgrains at subsidised rates to nearly 320 million people, sharply pushing up the country's food subsidy bill.
"The food subsidy bill will go up to 83 billion rupees ($2.31 billion) in 1997/98 (April-March) from 59 billion rupees in the current year," Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav told reporters.

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda told parliament earlier that for people living below the poverty line, the government proposed to sell through the public distribution system both common and fine rice at 3.50 rupees per kg, and wheat at 2.50 rupees per kg.
** The $272 billion ING group is setting up two dedicated funds and two regional investment funds with an estimted exposure of $300 million in India, the Business Standard says.
The paper says the group is also looking at investment

opportunitites in the country's real estate and insurance sectors and will soon apply to the Indian government for permission to set up a representative ofice for entry into the life insurance business.
** The Steel Authority of India (SAIL) is facing the spectre of substantially reduced profit margins for the first time in 10 years, the Economic Times reports.

The paper quoted SAIL Chairman, Arvind Pande as saying the profits of the country's largest steel producer are expected to be significantly lower than the 13.19 bllion rupees net profit posted n 1995/96.
** The rupee opened Tuesday at 35.89/90 per dollar against the previous close of 35.88/89, dealers said. Tuesday's range seen at 35.88/90 rupees to a dollar.
** A wave of fresh speculative selling ahead of Friday's 1997/98 annual budget pulled down Indian blue chips on Monday in nervous trade, dealers said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's 30-share index .BSESN tumbled 81.02 points, or 2.36 percent, to close at 3,358.47.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index .NSEI fell 26.80 points, or 2.7 percent, to 962.70.
** The Delhi share index .DE lost 7.31 points to 718.55.
** The Calcutta share index .CALSN was down 6.40 points at 440.51.
** The Madras share index .MDSI slumped 38.75 points to 3,321.90.
